newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Islamic states accuse Israel of reneging on peace.
newsitem.headline: Islamic states accuse Israel of reneging on peace.

text.p: Islamic nations accused Israel on Monday of reneging on its Middle East peace deal with the Palestinians and sought closer economic cooperation among themselves to further the welfare of the world's 1.5 billion Moslems.
The Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC), which opened its annual foreign ministers' meeting on Monday, also expanded its membership to 54 with the admission of Surinam.
But the ministers ignored the rival claims of Afghanistan's warring parties and left Kabul's seat vacant for the duration of the five-day meeting.
They also admitted the Central African Republic and Togo as observers, and set up a committee to assess criteria for OIC membership.

Indonesian President Suharto, leader of the world's most populous Islamic state, said in an opening address that the Palestinian people "continue to suffer Israel's acts of provocation as it reneges on its commitments under the 1993 Declaration of Principles and subsequent agreements".
"Agreements between Palestine and Israel are irrevocable international accords which cannot be changed and must be respected," he said.
Suharto added that for a just and comprehensive peace in the Middle East, "Israel must unconditionally withdraw from the Syrian Golan Heights and Southern Lebanon".
Indonesia's Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, who is chairing the 53-member OIC gathering, referred to "a dangerous impasse" in the Middle East.
Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara accused the Israeli government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of omitting "the peace plan from its plan of action".

Reporting on the day's sessions, Izhar Ibrahim, director general for political affairs at the Indonesian foreign ministry, said the ministers decided to leave Afghanistan's seat vacant "without prejudice to the question of the recognition of the government of Afghanistan".
The purist Islamic Taleban militia seized Kabul on September 27. Forces loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani and ethnic Uzbek leader Rashid Dostum are trying to retake the city.

"It is essential that the parties involved in the conflict initiate broad-based inter-Afghan talks aimed at establishing a government of national unity," conference chairman and Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said.
Other areas of concern include Bosnia-Herzegovina, Jammu and Kashmir, divided Cyprus and Somalia.
Conference sources said the troubled Russian territory of Chechnya and Greece had sought invitations to attend the OIC meeting, but it was not clear in what capacity.
Suharto in his address also called for a constructive North-South dialogue for global development and for OIC states to cooperate in economic growth and investment.
"We hope this will get a positive response from all sides and all members of the OIC," Indonesia's Ibrahim said.
Speakers also called for unity to put forward what Alatas called the true face of Islam.
He said there were dangerous misconceptions equating violence and terrorism with the Moslem world.

This would never be resolved, however, "until we are able to effectively communicate Islam for what it is -- a force for peace, justice and common good, a way of life that has intellectually enriched Western civilisation itself".
